# Results — Study 730 (Ferrari-F1)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test — **Ferrari's
stock (NYSE: RACE) gets a fan-sentiment / brand-halo "pop" the Monday after Scuderia
Ferrari wins a Formula 1 Grand Prix** — the Ferrari-specific cousin of the
Edmans-García-Norli sports-sentiment effect, on the one listed company whose brand *is* a
race team. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month).
Fingerprint `5e3d6de14719` (RACE + SPY, one combined panel).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (total-return) closes, `RACE` (Ferrari N.V., NYSE) + `SPY` (SPDR S&P 500), one combined panel: **2,701 rows, 2015-10-01 → 2026-06-30** |
| Instrument | `RACE` — Ferrari N.V., NYSE-listed 2015-10-21 at USD 52 (FCA separation completed 2016-01-03; Milan listing 2016-01-04). A USD, US-listed line → a US market benchmark is the fair counterfactual |
| Calendar | **hardcoded**: every Ferrari F1 Grand Prix **victory** in the RACE-listed era — **24 wins, 2017→2024** (Ferrari were **winless in 2016, 2020, 2021, 2025**). Source: STATS F1 "Ferrari — Wins" / Wikipedia "Ferrari Grand Prix results", each date cross-checked against Formula1.com season results |
| Events resolvable | **24 of 24** wins postdate the RACE listing and have RACE + SPY coverage around the race (11 in the 2017-18 "title-contender" era, 13 "sporadic") |
| Statistics | one-sample *t* of the abnormal return across independent, non-overlapping race events (the correct unit — not a daily panel); Wilson hit-rate interval; a 20-seed × 500-draw random-calendar placebo; Welch *t* for the contender-vs-sporadic contrast |
| Execution / costs | one documented convention: every Grand Prix runs **Sunday** (non-trading); **day(-1)** = last close before the race (does not know the result), **day(0)** = first close after (fully public, ~12-40h old, zero look-ahead). Signal = day(-1)→day(-1)+k; Tradability = day(0)→day(0)+k, net of 2× one-way cost × NAV |
| Independence quirk (named) | at the **day(0)** headline horizon all 24 wins are distinct Mondays → exact independence. At the **1-week** horizon three back-to-back win pairs overlap (Belgium/Monza 2019, Britain/Austria 2022, USA/Mexico 2024) — flagged, and the weekly cut is re-run dropping the second race of each pair |

**A note on the benchmark.** RACE trades in New York in USD, so `SPY` is the honest
market counterfactual: it strips the market-wide part of any given Monday move, leaving
the Ferrari-specific residual. An auto/luxury-peer benchmark (RACE vs a European luxury
basket) is the natural sequel and would sharpen the "brand-specific" reading — noted in
[references.md](references.md), not silently substituted here.

## The signal — abnormal return, day(-1) → day(-1)+k (RACE − SPY)

| cut | n | mean AR | *t* | hit rate (Wilson 95%) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **day(0) "win pop" (k=1)** | 24 | **+0.276%** | **+1.18** | 13/24 = 54.2% [35.1%, 72.1%] |
| 1 week (k=5) | 24 | +0.862% | +1.39 | 12/24 = 50.0% [31.4%, 68.6%] |
| 1 week, independent-only (drop 3 back-to-back 2nd races) | 21 | +1.314% | +2.29 | — |

The headline is the **day(0) pop** — the immediate Friday-close → Monday-close reaction,
the thing a "brand-halo" mechanism actually predicts, and the only fully non-overlapping
horizon. It is **+0.276%**, *t* = **+1.18**, with a **54.2%** hit rate whose Wilson
interval straddles a coin flip. The 1-week horizon drifts a little higher (*t* = +1.39);
the independence-corrected weekly cut clears the raw *t* ≥ 2 bar, but see the placebo and
the era split below before reading anything into it.

## Random-calendar placebo (20 seeds × 500 draws, right-tail)

| cut | observed mean | placebo mean (sd) | *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| day(0) pop | +0.276% | +0.032% (0.318%) | **0.214** |
| 1 week | +0.862% | +0.155% | 0.159 |
| 1 week, independent-only | +1.314% | — | 0.062 |

Redrawing the same 24 anchors at random points in RACE's own history reproduces the
observed day(0) mean **21% of the time** — a random Monday is statistically the same as a
Ferrari-win Monday. Even the independence-corrected weekly cut (raw *t* = 2.29) fails the
placebo at the 5% level (*p* = 0.062). No headline cut is unusual.

## Tradability — capture, day(0) → day(0)+k, net of costs

Entered at day(0)'s close (the first price *after* the result is public — zero look-ahead,
since the race runs on a non-trading Sunday), held one week.

| cut | gross | net @ 5 bps (*t*) | net @ 10 bps (*t*) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 week | +0.578% (*t* = +1.06) | +0.478% (+0.88) | +0.378% (+0.69) |

Random-calendar placebo on the net-of-cost capture: observed +0.478% vs placebo mean
+0.056% → **p = 0.274**. There is no edge to charge costs against in the first place; the
capture is a random-window draw. **Tradability = Mirage.**

## Contender vs sporadic — fan sentiment, or championship fundamentals?

The wins are pre-tagged in `data.py` by era: **contender** (2017-18, when a Vettel win
updated a live title fight — genuine fundamental/championship content) vs **sporadic**
(2019, 2022-24, one-off wins in seasons Ferrari finished well behind — the pure
"we-won-a-race" sentiment events the folklore is really about).

| era | n | day(0) mean | *t* | 1-week mean | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| contender (2017-18) | 11 | +0.386% | +1.04 | **+2.471%** | **+2.73** |
| sporadic (2019, 2022-24) | 13 | +0.183% | +0.59 | −0.499% | −0.74 |

Welch *t* (contender − sporadic): day(0) = **+0.42**, 1 week = **+2.63**.

The **only** cut in the whole study that clears both the raw *t* ≥ 2 bar *and* its own
placebo is the **contender-era 1-week drift**: +2.471%, *t* = 2.73, random-calendar
placebo **p = 0.017**. But it lives *entirely* in the two seasons when a Ferrari win
carried championship information, and it **reverses sign** for the sporadic wins that are
pure fan sentiment (−0.499%). Whatever little moves RACE around a win is tracking
**fundamentals** (a live title campaign), not **fan mood** — which is the opposite of the
claim. The effect, such as it is, is **misattributed**.

## Event anatomy — does the shape match "a win-day pop"?

Mean cumulative abnormal return by trading day from day(-1) (the pre-race anchor):

| day | 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| RACE − SPY | 0.000% | +0.276% | +0.287% | +0.649% | +0.969% | +0.862% |

A fan-sentiment reaction to a Sunday win should appear as a **jump on Monday (day 1)**
that then holds. Instead the Monday move is small (+0.276%) and the path drifts up only
over the following week — a shape that looks like ordinary single-name noise, not a
broadcast-night pop.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic paired (asset, benchmark) log-return world (ρ ≈ 0.55, like RACE vs SPY,
with single-name idiosyncratic vol > index vol) with a scheduled synthetic win calendar
and a TUNABLE planted "fan-halo bump"; no network.

| world | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (bump = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **+0.43** (sd 1.01), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** |
| planted bump = +1.0% (seed 730) | **+2.34** |
| planted bump = +2.0% (seed 730) | **+5.73** |

The detector recovers a planted bump and mostly does not fire on the null (1/20 seeds at
|t| ≥ 2, in line with the expected false-positive rate at this n — not a bias). *(A
faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The fan-sentiment "win pop" the folklore predicts — the immediate
  day(0) reaction — is a coin flip: AR **+0.276%**, *t* = **+1.18**, hit rate 54.2%,
  random-Monday placebo *p* = 0.214. No immediate-reaction cut clears *t* ≥ 2. The one
  raw-significant cut is a slow 1-week *drift* (not a pop), and it survives only in the
  title-contender subgroup — see the third axis.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** No cut clears *t* ≥ 2 net of costs with placebo confirmation;
  the best honest, zero-look-ahead trade is +0.478% net over a week (*t* = 0.88, placebo
  *p* = 0.274) — indistinguishable from a random window. There is no edge to size.
- **Fan-halo, or championship fundamentals? — MISATTRIBUTED.** The only signal that
  clears both bars (contender-era 1-week, *t* = 2.73, placebo *p* = 0.017) is confined to
  2017-18, when a Ferrari win updated a live championship; the pure sporadic wins show
  nothing (−0.499%, *t* = −0.74; Welch contender − sporadic = +2.63 at the week). What
  little moves RACE tracks fundamentals, not fans — the brand-halo story is the wrong
  label for it.
